question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=8$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{x-8}{4-\sqrt{2x}} & =\frac{8-8}{4-\sqrt{2\cdot 8}}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{x-8}{4-\sqrt{2x}} & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{(x-8)(4+\sqrt{2x})}{(4-\sqrt{2x})(4+\sqrt{2x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{(x-8)(4+\sqrt{2x})}{{4}^{2}-{(\sqrt{2x})}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{(x-8)(4+\sqrt{2x})}{16-2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{(x-8)(4+\sqrt{2x})}{-2(x-8)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {8}^{+}}\frac{4+\sqrt{2x}}{-2} \\  & =\frac{4+\sqrt{2(8)}}{-2} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
